newsitem.title: UK: AEA Technology sees interest cover falling.
newsitem.headline: AEA Technology sees interest cover falling.

text.p: British science and nuclear technology company AEA Technology Plc said on Monday it expected interest cover to fall from current levels of 21.9 times.
"We would expect to see interest cover come down (this year)...even into single figures but not into small single figures," finance director Ray Proctor told a press conference.
He said that the company could have between 15-20 million stg to spend if interest cover were allowed to slip to around 10 times from current levels.
"We've always made plain we are an acquisitive company," he added.
Some of this decrease would be as a result of investments, company executives added, as well as for bolstering partnerships.
Chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver stressed any acquisitions would have to be in areas which fitted with AEA Technology's existing business, however, but could be in the UK or overseas.

The company, spun off from the state-owned Atomic Energy Authority last year, earlier on Monday turned in a rise in annual pre-tax profits to 18.5 million stg from 15.8 million previously and paid out a total dividend of 8.4 pence per share.
It made three acquisitions last year for a total spend of 12.3 million stg.
It said its research and development spending of around 5.5 million stg last year, was likely to increase to 7.5 million.
At its engineering services division, margins were expected to improve this year after slipping to 6.5 percent from nine percent.
Proctor said the company was looking at declining volumes in the division and costs to improve the outlook.
